name: Saturn from Voyager 1, November 13, 1980
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 1's wide-angle camera through orange, green and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: A close view of part of Saturn, as a crescent, from about 1.2 million kilometers from Saturn's center, 18 hours after Voyager 1's closest approach to Saturn on November 12, 1980. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
